source: Royal Government of Cambodia, General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) / Boosting Food Production Program (PMO), "ខែ្សសង្វាក់ផលិតកម្ម ដំណាំពោតនៅកម្ពុជា" (Corn Production Value Chain in Cambodia), 2017
text:
For red corn grown in Battambang and Pailin provinces, the document diagrams a shorter value-chain flow (Figure 10 in the source), with only three main links:

Producers (farmers): sell either wet cob corn at farm-gate prices of about 600-700 riel/kg, or dried kernel corn at about 600-800 riel/kg -- the same farm-gate price range reported for Kampong Cham/Kandal.

District-level and in-community collectors: purchase corn in the local market, own their own weighing scales, negotiate price/volume directly with farmers, and arrange transport, sometimes with financing ties to particular villages or communities.

Exporters to Thailand: buyers based near the Thai border who purchase corn collected from Battambang and Pailin, buying based on price set by markets in Thailand, and who transport corn across the border into Thailand.

This Battambang/Pailin chain has one fewer intermediary step than the Kampong Cham/Kandal chain (which also includes domestic feed-mill factories as a parallel buying channel), reflecting Battambang and Pailin's proximity to the Thai border and stronger orientation toward direct cross-border export over domestic feed-mill sales.
